summary: Short call to align procurement, legal and engineering on the vendor gate path for Redwood's inference platform. Main threads: DPA redlines, egress fee exposure, SSO/KMS expectations, and acceptance criteria for a pilot. Agreed next steps include MSA updates and a follow-up technical benchmark artifact.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-23 15:00 PST · 55 minutes · attendees listed above

Summary auto-draft (may be imperfect): quick procurement + legal alignment on vendor gate. Some cross-talk about egress math and private deployment option.

00:00 Samira Patel (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, happy holidays, we'll try to keep this tight, quick agenda — redlines, egress math, pilot acceptance.
00:22 Aisha Rahman (Procurement): yes thanks Samira. we have a couple folks from legal and infra on. main ask is we need a clear path to signoff; what docs do we need, and what's the likely egress delta, ya know.
00:44 Tommy Lee (Counsel): hi, thanks. quick note, we usually require DPA language aligned with our template, and we have specific audit artifact needs for SOC2 scope. also curious about KMS keying and whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys.
01:10 Diego Morales (Redwood SE): quick call out — yes we support customer-managed K-M-S in Private and Dedicated flows; hosted has an HSM integration option. I'll be explicit in the doc. also, there are two main paths: hosted api with egress charged on cloud provider side, or Redwood Dedicated/Private where egress is controlled differently.
01:38 Ravi Menon (Platform Eng): can you explain the difference in egress billing flow? we pay egress at our cloud provider right now; do we pay double, or is it bundled?
02:05 Jules Tan (Redwood SA): good question. short version: with hosted API, your tenant traffic leaves our infra, egress is billed to us; we typically pass egress fees through as part of usage or separate carrier charge depending on region. with Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool) you have options: colocated in your VPC with private peering — in that case egress is usually your cloud provider's egress; Redwood may not bill additional egress beyond contractual network fees. (murmur) this is where the egress delta sits.
02:40 Maya Ortiz (FinOps): ok so we need a model: worst case egress + per-token cost inc, how big could that be for our expected workload of 200M tokens/month?
03:02 Diego: rough back-of-envelope — depends on sequence lengths; if you're doing average 1k tokens per request it's different. but we'll put together a cost sheet. I'll share a sample calc that shows hosted vs dedicated numbers.
03:28 Aisha: also on DPA redlines — our legal insists on data residency and deletion assurances for PII. how do you handle request logs and retention?
03:50 Samira: Redwood's standard DPA supports retention controls; we have options to limit logging, and we can offer retention windows aligned with your policy. for Private deployments you can opt to keep logs entirely on-prem.
04:08 Tommy: on the MSA side — our counsel rarely accepts open indemnities. we need to understand SLAs, outage timelines, and rollback. what are your standard SLA thresholds?
04:30 Diego: our Dedicated offering has SLA targets for latency and availability; we can propose an uptime SLA and a rollback policy to an alternative model in case of degradation. for hosted we have tiered SLOs. I'll attach the SLA matrix.
04:56 Ravi: question on KV cache and model variants — if you fallback to smaller model to save cost, does context quality degrade unacceptably for our use case?
05:15 Jules: good point. fallback policies are configurable per route; you can pin to a model version for pilot acceptance criteria. our Optimize team can suggest quantization profiles to preserve quality while reducing GPU memory.
05:40 Tommy: please be aware: our security policy requires RBAC + SSO via SAML and audit logs for every admin action; can Redwood show auth artifact and audit log samples?
06:02 Diego: yes we have SAML SSO integration and audit logging for token issuance and model updates; we'll include sample logs.
06:24 Maya: egress again — we have to present finance with a 3-scenario forecast: conservative, expected, stress. can you give us numbers for 3 scoping bands?
06:43 Samira: absolutely. action: Diego will produce a hosted vs dedicated cost model with conservative/expected/stress for tokens and egress.
07:05 Aisha: about pilot acceptance — we need pass/fail criteria: latency p95 under X ms, quality threshold using our prompt set, and no data residency exceptions. can we codify that?
07:30 Jules: yes, we usually accept an eval harness. propose: you hand over a 50-prompt test set, we'll run 5,000 calls and provide metrics p50/p95 latency, token costs, and quality regression score.
07:57 Ravi: timeline? we need this before the procurement committee Jan 20.
08:10 Samira: we can aim to have the benchmark packet in your hands by Dec 30, Redwood will send MSA redline by Jan 3, and follow up meeting in week of Jan 12 to triage legal comments.
08:32 Tommy: on DPA redlines we will push for stronger deletion language; is there precedent for limiting logs to 30 days?
08:48 Diego: for hosted it's typical to 90 days; shorter windows often require Private or Dedicated with log routing. we'll call that out.
09:05 Maya: if private deployment reduces egress exposure, what's the tradeoff in ops and cost?
09:25 Jules: Private means you run in your VPC or we ship an on-prem bundle; higher up-front for dedicated infra, but per-token cost can be lower and egress is controlled by you. however ops overhead and patch management are considerations.
09:50 Aisha: our vendor gate includes a privileged access review — will Redwood support PKI and limited admin roles?
10:10 Diego: yes, PKI for keying and granular RBAC are supported in Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports role-based controls and integration with your SSO provider.
10:32 Customer crosstalk: (unintelligible)
10:45 Tommy: another ask — audit artifacts for a SOC2: we need encryption-at-rest certs, key rotation docs, incident response playbook.
11:05 Jules: we'll provide the artifact list; note some items are only available in Dedicated/Private or under an enterprise package. we'll call out what's standard and what's add-on.
11:30 Maya: one more for FinOps — can you show how egress shows up on invoice? is it an explicit line item?
11:45 Samira: yes, typically explicit. but for some channel partners it may be embedded; we will provide sample invoice line items.
12:05 Ravi: okay, can we recap pilot acceptance one more time?
12:22 Samira: pilot acceptance: (1) legal DPA agreed, (2) bench tests p95 latency under agreed threshold, (3) quality regression below X% on your prompt set, (4) egress budget within band. that's the checklist we propose.
12:58 Aisha: sounds reasonable. any blockers for procurement?
13:15 Tommy: main blocker is DPA redlines and indemnity limits — we need the MSA language to review. also need clarity on rollback and disaster recovery.
13:42 Diego: we'll add draft rollback playbook and fallback model policy.
14:05 Maya: one detail — if we sign Dedicated and later want to move to Private on-prem, is migration supported?
14:28 Jules: yes, we support migration paths; there are data transfer costs and some manual config but it's a standard professional services engagement. we'll highlight that.
14:50 Aisha: can you include a short note on data residency and where our data might be stored in the hosted case?
15:12 Samira: hosted has region pins; we have EU, US West, US East. we'll specify default backup location and residency guarantees in the DPA draft.
15:35 Tommy: and encryption keys — confirm customer-managed keys for Dedicated, and HSM option for hosted?
15:55 Diego: correct. we'll document key lifecycle, rotation, and emergency key-rotation procedures.
16:20 Customer: (laugh) holiday small talk, thanks everyone.
16:40 Samira: ok last thing — egress worst-case example: Diego, can you provide a stress calc for 2B tokens/month and show the egress cost delta?
17:00 Diego: yes, I'll include a stress calc in the cost sheet. also will annotate assumptions: avg token bytes, response length, and req/resp ratio.
17:22 Aisha: perfect. can you also include competitor fallback notes: if we choose other vendor, what are the big tradeoffs?
17:40 Jules: we noted OpenAI and Vertex as competitors; the main diffs are SLA depth, private deployment support, and pricing transparency. we'll include a brief comparison.
17:58 Tommy: one more legal thing — we may ask for an audit right clause; are you ok with limited audit rights under NDA?
18:20 Samira: yes, we typically accept scoped audit rights under NDA; details in MSA.
18:42 Maya: great. thanks all. recap next steps?
19:00 Samira: recap: Samira send MSA redline (DPA callouts) by Jan 3; Diego to share dedicated vs hosted benchmarks and cost sheets by Dec 30; customer to confirm egress budget by Jan 10; follow-up meeting week of Jan 12.
19:28 Aisha: noted. thanks team. happy holidays.
19:40 End of recording.

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-heard acronyms (K-M-S, KV cache transcribed as K V), speakers sometimes generic. parts of the conversation redaction flagged for legal (PII examples) — handled out of band.
